title: Private deployment customer requests triage: networking & upgrade constraints playbook
creator: Asha Raman
description: Purpose: Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook for intake and prioritization of non-bug customer requests related to Private/VPC/on-prem deployments where networking constraints, upgrade windows, and air-gapped requirements are primary factors. Background: We continue to receive ad-hoc customer asks that require coordination across networking, security, and SRE teams. Without a standardized triage we surface inconsistent requests, slow response times, and missed upgrade commitments. This ticket codifies the intake checklist, a decision rubric, and an escalation path so Sales/SE/Support can set consistent expectations and PM can prioritize engineering work against Dedicated and Private roadmaps.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page intake form (Confluence + support template) for networking/air-gap/upgrade requests that captures minimum required artifacts (network diagram, maintenance window, KMS/HSM details, allowed egress/ingress CIDRs)
A documented triage rubric with numeric scoring for urgency, upgrade complexity, security exposure, and customer strategic value
A published routing table mapping request scores to outcomes (self-serve docs, SRE runbook, follow-up with Solutions Engineering, or blocked until architecture review)
An initial pilot with 3 enterprise customers completed and post-pilot feedback captured
Stakeholder sign-off from Security, SRE, Solutions Engineering, and Sales Engineering
triage_rubric: Upgrade window constraint: 0-4 (0=no constraint, 4=must be airgap with manual upgrade only)
Network complexity: 0-5 (based on number of firewalls, NATs, cross-region peering, private endpoints)
Data sensitivity/security exposure: 0-5 (includes encryption, KMS/HSM, compliance requirements)
Operational effort estimate: 0-8 (rough Eng + SRE days)
proposed_flow: 1) Intake: Support/SE fills the standardized form and attaches network diagram and maintenance SLA
2) Triage: PM or assigned intake coordinator scores request within 24 business hours using rubric
3) Route: Based on score, auto-assign to one of: (a) self-serve docs + SE assist, (b) Solutions Eng deep-dive + SRE schedule, (c) Engineering backlog for product work
4) Scheduling: If an upgrade or on-prem install is required, SRE proposes 3 candidate maintenance windows; approval needed from customer and Security
5) Execution: Runbook handed to SRE/Deploy team; post-upgrade checklist and smoke tests required
6) Postmortem: For any incident or failed upgrade, produce a 72-hour summary and update the intake form checklist
tradeoffs: Speed vs safety: Allowing faster on-site upgrades increases risk of missed steps; mitigated by mandatory runbook items but slows delivery
Standardization vs flexibility: A strict intake form reduces ambiguity but may frustrate customers with bespoke architectures
Implementation cost: Building full automation for air-gapped installs is expensive vs executing manual playbooks per customer
